articles.title: Denehurst Park café opens in restored Victorian manor house on September 5
articles.excerpt: Denehurst House, a restored Victorian manor in Denehurst Park, opens as a café on 5 September, managed by veterans' group Get Together After Serving.
articles.content_html:
A 19th century manor house in Rochdale has been transformed into a café, which will officially open on Saturday, 5 September. Denehurst House, located in Denehurst Park, has been renovated after lying empty for decades and will now serve as a community hub for local residents and veterans.

The café will be managed by the Community Interest Company Get Together After Serving (GTAS), which is staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families. Founded by Rochdale residents Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor, and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community through various wellbeing programmes and events.

Visitors to the café can expect a menu featuring hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts, and a selection of teas and coffees. The café will also collaborate with local businesses to offer special menu items on Fridays, such as curry, pizza, and pies. The café's opening hours will be from 9am to 6pm daily between May and October, and from 9am to 4pm between November and April.

Rochdale Borough Council, which owns Denehurst House, commissioned local builders H Bell and Sons for the renovation, ensuring that the building's period features, including ornate coving and bay windows, were preserved. The council is also considering using the upper floors of the building for accommodation for local veterans, following a recent public consultation on the proposal. Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for housing and regeneration, expressed enthusiasm for the project, highlighting its importance to the community.
